content:
Decent puzzle. I think validators 1 and 2 should be swapped so that both pair 2 cases test the 'equal' part of 'less than or equal to'.
It might also be fun to include cases where the maximum food level is 0, or even negative (although that wouldn't make sense). Perhaps a pair where n=0 as well?

✅ Approved the contribution.
Comment: A good puzzle for clash of code, the goal is cristal clear and tests cover all case.
it is really good as basic, like I used simply if else and ascii code to solve it.
Thank you for the feedback. This is my first contribution, so I really appreciate it.
Withdrawing my approval — I approved too quickly without checking the issues raised by 5DN1L. The Goal section and the Input/Output format need reworking first.

Goal
* Please explain the exact relationship between hungerPoints and food name instead of giving examples.

* Please format all the percentages and possible output phrases as {{constants}}.

Input / Output
* Please study the example on this page: https://www.codingame.com/playgrounds/40701/help-center/statement , and rewrite the Input and Output sections following the example there.

Cases
* In the Garden (Test 2): Please remove the trailing newline from the input.

* Q Time! (Validator 3): Please remove or replace the non-ASCII character "é" from the input.

* Each test and its corresponding validator should cover the same scenario (i.e. same expected output) with slightly different inputs. Please regroup the existing cases and add additional cases accordingly.

Thanks.
Fixed the issues you pointed out. Thank you for your help!
Fixed the issues 5DN1L pointed out. Thank you for your help!

It's definitely solvable in less than 5 minutes. There's a few things you have done the hard way. I'll point out the main parts here and then try to PM you my code.

Your elif statements are checking for conditions twice. ie. 'if fp<=0.2*m' means that anything that reaches the next condition is greater than 0.2*m, so no need to include that in the elif.

The constraints state that the first letter of each item is uppercase, so converting the item to lowercase is unnecessary.

Look into ord() and chr().

Print statements can contain if's and else's, turning your last 12 lines into 1.
I've sent my code via PM in the forum. I think you'll have to go there to find it.
There are still some issues. I'll comment again.

Thank you for the update. There are still a number of issues to address:

General
* It's a bit odd to use "hungerPoints" as the variable name when a higher value generally (though not absolutely) means "more food has been eaten" rather than "hungrier". Consider using another name like "foodPoints" instead?

Goal
* Consider removing the word "previous" from the first paragraph.

* The revised third paragraph is slightly better, but it still doesn't explain the rule in a concrete way. Please rewrite it as follows:

For every [[food]], its [[hungerPoints]] is equal to the position (1-based) of its first letter in the English alphabet. That is, {{A}} = {{1}}, {{B}} = {{2}} and so on, up to {{Z}} = {{26}}.

Input
* Please format "Line 1", "Line 2" and "Next [[n]] lines" in <<bold>>.

* Please move "Each [[food]] consists of letters without spaces." to the Constraints section, replacing the third constraint.

Output
* Please change "Output" to "<<Line 1>>:".

* Please change ":" to "." and remove all the points below; there's no need to repeat the conditions.

Constraints
* Please add a constraint to state the lower and upper bounds on the length of [[food]].

Cases
* Q Time? (Test 7): Please remove the hyphen from "Quatre-epices" as it's not a letter, violating the constraint that food names contain letters only.

* Please add these cases to cover currently missing features:

  • Test 9: The input should include food names starting with U, X and Y (and other letters if you like). The output should be "Just a little bit."

  • Validator 9: The input should include food names starting with F, G, H, J, M, U, V, X and Y (and other letters if you like). The output should be "Just a little bit."
Fixed all the bugs you brought up. Once again, thank you for the help!

We're almost there. Just two more changes:

Constraints
* Please add: 1 ≤ length of [[food]] ≤ 20

Stub generator
* Please change 100 to 20.

Thanks.
